children: The transaction involves nearly the entire stake held by Mastercard Asia/Pacific, following the fintech’s listing on Indian stock exchanges last year

Shares of Pine Labs rose more than 2 per cent on Tuesday, 22 September, after 4.97 crore shares, representing about 4.3 per cent of the fintech company’s equity, changed hands through a block deal. The transaction follows reports that Mastercard Asia/Pacific Pte. Ltd. was seeking to sell its entire holding in Pine Labs for nearly Rs 900 crore, with the large trade putting the company’s ownership structure in focus.

The stock was trading at Rs 198.66 in morning deals, up 2.56 per cent from its previous close of Rs 193.70. The identity of the buyer and seller in Tuesday’s transaction was not immediately available. However, Mastercard’s disclosed holding as of June 2026 was 4.97 crore shares, or a 4.31 per cent stake, broadly matching the quantity involved in the block deal.

The proposed transaction had a floor price of Rs 179.50 per share, representing a discount of about 7.3 per cent to Pine Labs’ previous closing price. At the floor price, the deal was valued at around Rs 892 crore. Citigroup Global Markets India acted as the sole placement agent for the transaction.

Mastercard first invested in Pine Labs in 2020 and subsequently sold part of its holding through Pine Labs’ initial public offering (IPO) in 2025. If Tuesday’s transaction is confirmed as Mastercard’s sale, it would mark the payments company’s exit from its remaining investment in Pine Labs.

Despite the sizable transaction and the discount indicated by the block deal floor price, Pine Labs shares moved higher during morning trade. At Rs 198.66, the stock was around 11 per cent above the reported floor price of Rs 179.50.

Pine Labs shares have declined 18.1 per cent so far in 2026, compared with a 10.5 per cent fall in the Nifty 50 over the same period. The company had a market capitalisation of around Rs 22,350 crore based on Monday’s closing price.

Pine Labs reported a net profit of Rs 19.6 crore for the April to June quarter, more than four times the Rs 4.8 crore recorded in the year ago period. Revenue from operations increased 19.6 per cent during the quarter, supported by increased adoption of digital payments and payments infrastructure.
